svg.text: The verb: write it true
Look at the wish, touch cards to hear them, lay them on the ribbon, touch the star. The world does exactly what the sentence says
1. The wish
2. The cards speak
3. Write it
4. It comes true
a picture, never words; Hoot says
"Someone's hungry for cheese!"
"mice"
each card says its word when touched;
the badge shows ONE mouse on all three
Three mice ate the cheese ★
(the frame's words are written on the ribbon too)
the star lights when every gap is full;
a touch casts (in VR: the Magic Wand)
T
h

Hoot reads it, each word lighting;
the ink flies; the meadow blooms
The Jumble's word: "three mouses"
ta-da!
A made-up word is a card like any other (it must be heard or read to be
told apart). Cast, it brings the Jumble out of the inkwell instead of mice:
it giggles, sneezes ink and hops home. Hoot: "Oops! That's not a real word."
Then: "One mouse, two mice. Some words change inside." The ink flows back;
nothing is spoilt. A wrong cast costs only that wish's first-time star.
Why only the first cast counts
If the ribbon showed what a spell would do before
the star, or if second casts counted, trying cards
until it looks right would win: the model's
trial-and-error player then reaches the bar on 100 %
of visits. With the first cast counting and no preview,
0 %: the form has to be chosen, which is the grammar.
